capture.original_context: My notes from the theory lesson. A semitone is the smallest step on the piano, from one key to the very next key. A major third spans four semitones, for example C to E. A minor third spans three semitones, for example C to E-flat. A major triad stacks a major third and then a minor third: C, E, G. A minor triad stacks a minor third and then a major third: C, E-flat, G. An octave doubles the frequency: A4 is 440 Hz and A5 is 880 Hz.
capture.original_input: Why is C to E a major third but C to E-flat a minor third? I keep mixing up thirds and triads.

learner_goal: Tell major and minor triads apart by counting semitones.

items.distinction: Count the semitones from the root to the middle note: four makes a major triad, three makes a minor triad.
